processes: Spotting an outlier in a plot
Judging whether to keep or question it
plainLanguageExplanation: An outlier is a data point that sits far away from the rest of the dataset — one lonely house price among modest ones, one giant storm in a calm year. It may be a real observation or an error like a typing mistake, and you must look at it carefully. An outlier distorts the mean (because it is added to the total) and the range (because it stretches the extremes), while leaving the median almost untouched. Scientists record it rather than hide it, but then must decide whether it's a rare true event or an error to drop.

whyItMatters: Outliers can be the most interesting points in a dataset — a customer with a huge order, a machine that broke, a star athlete. Knowing how they shift your summaries and when to keep or question them is honest statistics.
tagline: The point far from the crowd
didYouKnow: Outliers have scientific gold in them — the planet Neptune was found because astronomers studied a strange irregularity (an outlier) in Uranus's orbit and asked what could explain it.
compareReason: Students don't realize one point could bend their 'average' — comparing the outlier's effect on mean vs. median makes robustness real.
